questions.q: What does it mean that the Azure SDK for Python and Boto3 are "official" SDKs?
options: They're identical to the REST API documentation with no actual code
They were built once and have never been updated since
They only work inside each company's own internal tools, never in a standalone script
They're maintained directly by Microsoft and Amazon themselves, kept in sync with new service features, not community-built wrappers
questions.explain: An official SDK is updated by the cloud provider itself the moment a new feature ships, rather than by a volunteer reverse-engineering the REST API.

questions.q: Why is Python's cross-platform nature specifically useful for cloud automation?
options: The exact same script runs unmodified on Windows, Linux, and macOS
Cross-platform means it can only run inside a web browser
It has no relevance to automation work at all
Python only runs on Linux, which is why cloud providers prefer it
questions.explain: A script written once in Python runs the same way regardless of the operating system it's executed on, unlike some shell tooling.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what kind of task does Python handle better than a short shell script?
options: Printing a single line of text to the console
Tasks that never need to be run more than once
Running exactly one command with no conditions
Tasks needing real branching logic, structured data, and error handling across many resources
questions.explain: Python's dictionaries, lists, classes, and exception handling keep genuinely complex, multi-branch automation manageable in a way a growing shell script usually doesn't.

questions.q: Which real example shows Python already running "under the hood" of tools used earlier in this course?
options: Cloud CLIs have no underlying implementation language
The az CLI itself is written in Python, built on the Azure SDK for Python
The az CLI is written entirely in PowerShell
PowerShell is secretly a Python interpreter
questions.explain: The az CLI from Chapter 4 and AWS's own CLI (built on botocore) are both Python under the hood, as are Ansible's modules.

questions.q: Does choosing Python in this chapter mean PowerShell, taught in Chapters 1-2, is no longer useful?
options: Yes — PowerShell cannot be used for Azure automation anymore
No — Python adds a tool suited to more complex jobs; PowerShell and the CLI still have their place
No — but only because PowerShell is being deprecated by Microsoft
Yes — Python always replaces PowerShell entirely once it's introduced
questions.explain: This lesson is explicit: Python isn't declared a winner over PowerShell — it's a different tool that fits different, often more complex, jobs.
